stanzas: ... ]ὁμοῦ, πᾶσαι τε Θεοῦ λόγιμοι δε …? ι … ? [… ὅσα κ[όσμος]
... o]ὐ τὰν ἠῶ σιγάτω, μηδ᾿ ἄστρα φαεσφόρα χ[..]δε–
[σ]θων [ἐκ]λειπ[όντων] ῥ[ιπαὶ πνοιῶν, πηγαὶ] ποταμῶν ῥοθίων πᾶσαι. ὑμνούντων δ᾿ἡμῶν
[π]ατέρα χυἱὸν χἅγιον πνεῦμα, πᾶσαι δυνάμεις ἐπιφωνούντων ἀμὴν ἀμήν, κράτος αἶνος
[ἀεὶ καὶ δόξα Θεῷ] δ[ωτ]ῆ[ρι] μόνω[ι] [πάν]των ἀγαθῶν, ἀμὴν ἀμήν.
orig.credit: Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 1786 (late 3rd century), in Charles Cosgrove's edition (2011) as quoted in Wikipedia's article; square brackets mark letters restored by editors

stanzas: … together, all the eminent ones of God … [all that the] w[orld holds] …
… [neither night] nor dawn: let it be silent; let not the light-bearing stars [fall be-]
[hind,] let the rushing winds and all the springs of roaring rivers cease. While we sing
of Father and Son and Holy Spirit, let all the powers answer: Amen, amen. Power, praise
[always, and glory to God], the only giver of all good things. Amen, amen.
… ]homou, pasai te Theou logimoi de …? i … ? [… hosa k[osmos]
… o]u tan ēō sigatō, mēd' astra phaesphora ch[..]de–
[s]thōn [ek]leip[ontōn] rh[ipai pnoiōn, pēgai] potamōn rhothiōn pasai. hymnountōn d' hēmōn
[p]atera ch' hyion ch' hagion pneuma, pasai dynameis epiphōnountōn amēn amēn, kratos ainos
[aei kai doxa Theōi] d[ōt]ē[ri] monō[i] [pan]tōn agathōn, amēn amēn.

notes: The beginning of the papyrus is lost, so the hymn starts mid-sentence. Square brackets mark letters and words restored by editors; dots and question marks, letters that cannot be read.
Lines 2–3: the scribe broke a word across the line ("…de– / [s]thōn"), so the English runs over too.
Above the words the papyrus carries the melody in Greek vocal notation: the oldest surviving Christian hymn with its music.
